questions.problem: Suppose $A$ is a $5\times 5$ matrix and $det(A)=5.$ The matrix $B$ is obtained from $A$ by applying the elementary row operations ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}$ and ${R}_{3}:=3{R}_{3}.$ What is the value of $det(B)?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's figure out what each operation does to the determinant.

- The operation ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}$ involves swapping two rows, so it changes the sign of the determinant to the opposite one.

- The operation ${R}_{3}:=3{R}_{3}$ involves multiplying a row by $3,$ so the determinant is multiplied by $3$ as well.

Therefore, we have to change the sign of the determinant to the opposite one and multiply by $3$ as well. Consequently, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B) & =3\cdot (-det(A)) \\  & =-3det(A) \\  & =-3\cdot 5 \\  & =-15.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Suppose $Y$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $det(Y)=-3.$ What is the value of $det(4Y)?$
questions.worked_solution:
Multiplying a $n\times n$ matrix by a scalar $k$ is equivalent to multiplying each row by $k,$ and this occurs $n$ times. This leads to the result

$$
\begin{aligned}det(k\cdot Y)={k}^{n}\cdot det(Y).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have $k=4$ and $n=3.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}det(4Y) & ={4}^{3}\cdot det(Y) \\  & =64\cdot (-3) \\  & =-192.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Suppose $X$ is a $6\times 6$ matrix and $det(X)=28.$ The matrix $Y$ is obtained from $X$ by applying the elementary row operations ${R}_{1}:=\frac{3}{4}{R}_{1}$ and ${R}_{6}:={R}_{6}+(-7){R}_{2}.$ What is the value of $det(Y)?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's figure out what each operation does to the determinant.

- The operation ${R}_{6}:={R}_{6}+(-7){R}_{2}$ involves adding a multiple of one row to another row,  so it does not change the determinant.

- The operation ${R}_{1}:=\frac{3}{4}{R}_{1}$ involves multiplying a row by $\frac{3}{4},$ so the determinant is multiplied by $\frac{3}{4}$ as well.

Therefore, we only have to multiply the determinant by $\frac{3}{4}.$ Consequently, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}det(Y) & =\frac{3}{4}det(X) \\  & =\frac{3}{4}\cdot 28 \\  & =21.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that $det(A)=det(B),$ which of the following elementary row operations transforms matrix $A$ to matrix $B,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 3 \\ 3 & -5 & 6 \\ 2 & 3 & 5\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 3 \\ 3 & -5 & 6 \\ 0 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}]?
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $det(A)=det(B)$, the row operation applied to $A$ must be to add or subtract a multiple of one row to another row. In other words, it is of the form 

$$
{R}_{j}:={R}_{j}+(k){R}_{i},\,i\ne j.
$$

By considering the given row operations that are of the above form, we notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 3 \\ 3 & -5 & 6 \\ 2 & 3 & 5\end{aligned}| & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 3 \\ 3 & -5 & 6 \\ 0 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =det(B).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1}.
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the matrices given below. Given that $X$ and $Y$ are row equivalent matrices and $det(X)=5$, find $det(Y).$

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -2 \\ -3 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}],\,Y=[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 1 \\ -3 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that $Y$ can be obtained from $X$ by swapping the $2$nd and the $3$rd rows. 

This changes the sign of the determinant to the opposite one.
Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}det(Y) & =-det(X) \\  & =-(5) \\  & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$
